title: 2013 HMMT November Team Problem 5
statement: In triangle \(A B C, \angle B A C=60^{\circ}\). Let \(\omega\) be a circle tangent to segment \(A B\) at point \(D\) and segment \(A C\) at point \(E\). Suppose \(\omega\) intersects segment \(B C\) at points \(F\) and \(G\) such that \(F\) lies in between \(B\) and \(G\). Given that \(A D=F G=4\) and \(B F=\frac{1}{2}\), find the length of \(C G\).

solutions.text:
\(\boxed{\frac{16}{5}}\) Let \(x=CG\). First, by power of a point, \(BD = \sqrt{BF(BF+FG)}=\frac{3}{2}\), and \(C E=\sqrt{x(x+4)}\). By the law of cosines, we have

\[\left(x+\frac{9}{2}\right)^{2}=\left(\frac{11}{2}\right)^{2}+(4+\sqrt{x(x+4)})^{2}-\frac{11}{2}(4+\sqrt{x(x+4)})\]

which rearranges to \(2(5 x-4)=5 \sqrt{x(x+4)}\). Squaring and noting \(x>\frac{4}{5}\) gives \((5 x-16)(15 x-4)=\) \(0 \Longrightarrow x=\frac{16}{5}\).
